No ADORE split file is opened anywhere in the file. Join of sentinel_data/processed/adore/split_assignments.parquet (assignment=='test') to the sealed label-free split, keys only: the four partitions the reviewers name = 11,157 ids -> 10,473 rows inside the universe = 2,465 of T1_test (23.37%) + 8,008 of train_pool (13.41%), 0 in T6a/T6b. Per partition: t-F2F/split_occurrence 4,133 ids -> 913 T1_test + 2,859 train_pool; t-F2F/split_scaffold-murcko -> 1,121 + 3,117; t-C2C/split_occurrence -> 186 + 784; a-CA2F-diff/split_occurrence -> 591 + 2,756. Governing text: sota_campaign.md rule 1; RESEARCH_PLAN §15.5 item 1 ('a test block already scored (M4 ADORE) cannot be re-used for a claim') and item 7 ('additions to a training set never include rows of any frozen test block'). verdicts.ruling_text: The stamp is withheld: before any stamp the builder must subtract, as a counted assertion, the union of the result_ids of every ADORE test partition that carries a scored row in results/registry.jsonl (t-F2F x split_occurrence and x split_scaffold-murcko, t-C2C x split_occurrence and x split_scaffold-murcko, t-A2A x split_occurrence and x split_scaffold-murcko, a-CA2F-same x split_occurrence, a-CA2F-diff x split_occurrence), freeze that id list with its own sha256 in §2, and re-derive the cluster file, the partition, the §3 table and every MDE from the reduced universe, with the old version preserved as _v1.

verdicts.evidence: sentinel/models/chemtox/unseen_taxa.py l.672-673: eA = rng.normal(0, rmse_level, len(y)); eB = r*eA + sqrt(1-r^2)*rng.normal(0, rmse_level, len(y)) — one independent draw PER ROW, zero within-cluster correlation, so cluster resampling recovers row-level variance. Numerically decisive: for all 12 cases in t1t6_mde.json the declared MDE matches 1.96*1.2*sqrt(1-0.81)/sqrt(n_rows) and is 2.5-5x smaller than the same formula on n_units. T1_test all: declared 0.0097, row formula 0.0100, unit formula 0.0474. T6a_test all: 0.0085 / 0.0090 / 0.0268. T6b_test all: 0.0197 / 0.0209 / 0.0532. §6's sentence 'so 85,746 rows from 11k (chemical, species) pairs are never treated as independent' is therefore false of these numbers, and §12.1(f) — the binding claim gate — and the §7.2 A1 attribution test are set 2.5-5x too lax. The target-invariance is genuine and separate (pA-y = eA, y cancels; the 1e-12 zeroed-target assertion at compute_t1t6_mde.py l.68-69 is real and all 12 cases record target_blind_identical=True), so this is a power error, not a leak.
verdicts.ruling_text: Before the stamp the MDE is recomputed with a within-unit error component reported at icc = 0.5 and icc = 1.0 alongside the current icc = 0 figures; until that table exists, condition (f) and the §7.2 A1 attribution test are gated at the unit-level rho=0.9 value (>= 0.047 T1_test, >= 0.027 T6a_test, >= 0.053 T6b_test), and the sentences 'Every block is better powered than T2's best (0.011)' and 'better powered than any block M4 has ever scored' are struck.

verdicts.evidence: build_t1t6_split.py l.152 computes sd_target from log10_conc_mol_L for every block including the three sealed ones; l.186-193 computes each test block's pooled within-group replicate floor from the same column. t1t6_counts.json records sd_target 1.7415 / 1.6806 / 1.7678 and replicate_floor 0.4954 / 0.4083 / 0.4578 for T1_test / T6a_test / T6b_test — exactly the figures printed in the amendment's §3 table (l.120-122) and §6 (l.312). t1t6_mde.json additionally records sd_target for all 12 cases (1.7414 / 1.8339 / 1.6805 / 1.7259 / 1.7675 / 1.7564 across block x stratum), i.e. the labels of the sealed blocks were read per stratum as well as per block. LEAD_DECISIONS_20261110.md rule 2 permits 'build data (labels of protected rows: counts only)'. The file's own §6 ('From counts and metadata only ... no label of any future test row informed any number in this table') is true of the MDE column only, and §13's forbidden list ('any read of T1_test, T6a_test or T6b_test beyond the row counts in §3') is written so that it exempts the read that had already happened. The read cannot be undone by a ruling, so the file must not be stamped while it presents these as counts-only.
verdicts.ruling_text: The stamp is withheld until §3 and §6 carry no label-derived statistic of T1_test, T6a_test or T6b_test (the SD(target) and per-test-block replicate-floor columns are struck; only the train_pool floor 0.504 may be cited as an absolute bound) and t1t6_counts.json and t1t6_mde.json are re-emitted without sd_target and per-test-block replicate_floor; the pre-stamp read is recorded as a disclosed deviation naming which design choices (cutoff 0.4, the 15% block, the duration bands, T6a/T6b status) were fixed before those statistics existed, and no further label-derived quantity of a sealed block is computed before its FREEZE file exists.

verdicts.evidence: §10.1 l.446-449 filters auxiliary rows by prospective result_id and T2 class only; grep of the whole amendment for 'parent' and for any cluster condition on H2/H3/H4 returns nothing. Counted from processed/ecotox/ecotox_aquatic.parquet after applying the amendment's own two subtractions, keys and counts only (no label value read): H3 chronic (NOEC/LOEC/EC10/MATC/NOEL/LOEL, value+smiles) = 30,160 rows on 455 held-out-cluster chemicals, 29,604 of them on 436 T1_test chemicals; H2 censored acute = 1,356 rows on 235 held-out chemicals, 1,319 on 225 T1_test chemicals. Auxiliary rows in the SAME (CAS, species, duration) cell as a sealed row: T1_test 4,895 chronic + 342 censored; T6a_test 11,773 + 551; T6b_test 2,209 + 72. Duration leak: H3 chronic rows on train_pool chemicals = 138,341, of which 84,812 are outside 24-96 h and 72,900 are above 96 h, on 973 pool chemicals, max duration 26,298 h — identical to T6a_test's maximum. §9 shows the same hole for H4 (588 of 672 chemicals in the universe, 456 in the pool). Project precedent is far stricter: sentinel/models/chemtox/aux.py l.3-11 and excluded_keys()/assert_no_test_chemicals() exclude by CAS and InChIKey every chemical in ANY test partition, 'because the ADORE core *is* ECOTOX'. This destroys T1's 'a chemical nobody has tested' premise (§1) and falsifies §3/§7.1's 'the pool is in-window only, selection extrapolates at most 2x'.
verdicts.ruling_text: Before the stamp §10.1 must state, and the loader must enforce as a counted assertion, that no auxiliary, multitask, pretraining or ablation row (H2, H3, H4, H5 and any future auxiliary target, for ted, R2, R3, mmoe, A4 and A5) whose test_cas falls in a held-out t1_cluster, or whose parent_key family touches a held-out cluster, or which shares a (CAS, species, duration) cell with a sealed row, enters any training set on either track; for every T6 entry the auxiliary rows are additionally restricted to 24 <= duration_h <= 96; the filtered row counts replace the §10.1 figures; and the H5 ACR target is computed from train_pool rows only.

verdicts.evidence: All eight §2 hashes verify on disk (cluster CSV a6e33634..., split 005f7957..., builder 6fb9ed52..., counts 1c443fed..., MDE c38a147d..., MDE script 2c171c0a..., H4 JSON 3ceead2f..., H4 script 0659b5f7...) and the sealed split is 0444 with exactly the five declared columns and 85,746 rows. verdicts.ruling_text: Before the stamp the author supplies a builder that deterministically emits the sealed label-free five-column split and the cluster file at their pinned paths and names with the column trim inside the script, re-pins the counts and MDE reports so that no artefact path lies in a temporary directory, and seals or deletes the eight-column label-carrying intermediate (and any copy) with its removal recorded; the stamp then re-verifies every §2 hash.

verdicts.evidence: sentinel/models/chemtox/unseen_taxa_guard.py l.34-38 hard-wires PLAN/PINS/DATA_DIR='processed/chemtox_unseen_taxa'/EXPERIMENT='chemtox_unseen_taxa_test'/BLOCKS=('insects','molluscs','amphibians'); load_test_block() (l.166-172) calls require_authorised(block) and then reads only test_blocks.parquet, so load_test_block('T1_test') cannot serve a new block. verify_freeze() (l.76-88) refuses if the pinned plan, guard or module sha changes, and chemtox_unseen_taxa_pins.json pins guard_sha256 e3721450... and module_sha256 cf1493c6..., both equal to the files on disk — so the guard cannot be edited without breaking T2's pending look, which the amendment's preamble also forbids. No T1/T6 code exists (sentinel/models/chemtox/ holds no arch-v2 module; sentinel_runs/chemtox/arch_v2 holds only six reports/scripts). Because the sealed split is label-free, the sealed rows' labels remain in processed/ecotox/ecotox_aquatic.parquet, which 7 modules read directly (scripts/data/{chemtox_build_prospective,chemtox_build_unseen_taxa,build_ecotox,build_chemicals}.py, sentinel/models/chemtox/{prospective,aux}.py, tests/test_chemtox_models.py). §8's 'load_test_block as the only reader' is therefore not true of the new blocks. Reviewer called this blocking; it is closable by a lead sentence that withholds look-clearance, so should_fix.
verdicts.ruling_text: This stamp clears no fit, no embedding run and no look on T1_test, T6a_test or T6b_test until a separate guard module with its own pins file, its own experiment key, the lead-written FREEZE check, BaseException abort, import-closure code hash, artefact verification and sealing, plus a protected labels artefact holding only the three blocks' targets, exist and have been reviewed; unseen_taxa_guard.py and unseen_taxa.py are not edited, and every T1/T6 loader reads rows through the new guard's pool loader rather than ecotox_aquatic.parquet.

verdicts.evidence: Reproduced with the project's own helper sentinel.models.chemtox.prospective.parent_key over docs/preregistration/chemtox_t1_clusters_v1.csv (3,893 of 3,895 SMILES resolve): 34 parent_keys span held-out and retained clusters, covering 130 chemicals and 92 clusters; joined to the sealed split that is 5,320 train_pool rows, 1,170 T1_test rows and 345 T6b_test rows. T1_test rows sharing a parent structure with a train_pool chemical: 1,170 of 10,548 = 11.09% (43 chemicals); T6b_test 345 of 2,410 = 14.32%. Precedent in the same workstream: chemtox_prospective_plan.md §4.5 (l.524-542) pre-registers a parent-structure-clustered sensitivity CI and a strict parent_novel co-primary track, and chemtox_unseen_taxa_plan.md §6 requires 'a parent-structure-clustered sensitivity CI for every primary comparison' and makes the parent_novel stratum a claim condition (f). grep -n parent on the amendment returns nothing.
verdicts.ruling_text: Either whole parent_key families are held out with their clusters and the partition re-derived, or, if the lead keeps the current split, the amendment pre-registers before the stamp a parent-structure-clustered co-primary CI and a 'parent-unseen' stratum with its row counts and its own MDE, and every T1 and T6b claim must hold in that stratum.

verdicts.evidence: sentinel/models/chemtox/chemprop_model.py pretrain_ecotox_encoder (l.~140-192): the docstring states rows 'must already have the evaluated challenge's test chemicals removed' and exclude_cas/exclude_inchikey remove only 'the current CV fold's validation chemicals'; the disk cache key covers 'the architecture, the pretraining settings and the excluded fold' — not the T1/T6 split. aux.py ecotox_auxiliary excludes only excluded_keys(primary_challenge). /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/sentinel_runs/chemtox/pretrained holds 20 ecotox_mp_*.pt checkpoints dated 2026-10-22, i.e. 19 days before the T1/T6 split existed, plus chemeleon_mp.pt (2026-10-22). Re-using any of them to initialise ted or rx_chemprop would put T1_test/T6a/T6b rows into pretraining. The reviewer's separate point that the frozen CheMeleon/MolFormer/ChemBERTa embeddings are structure-only and leak no label is correct and is a disclosure, not a leak.
verdicts.ruling_text: No checkpoint, embedding cache or auxiliary row set built before the T1/T6 split may initialise or feed any T1/T6 fit: pretraining rows are re-derived from block == train_pool after the AUX-LEAK exclusions, the cache key records the split file's sha256, and the amendment states as a disclosed limitation that the frozen pretrained embeddings saw the held-out structures (no labels).

verdicts.evidence: Substance confirmed, one figure refuted. From the sealed split: T1_test and T6b_test share 232 chemicals (of T6b's 278) and 181 clusters, and 0 rows — ST-6's '232 of 278' is right; CT-L8's '727 chemicals shared between T1_test and T6b_test' is wrong (727 is the count of held-out-cluster chemicals overall) and its '490 held-out clusters / T1 468 / T6b 203' framing is right. §12.1(c) says only 'Holm correction across the candidate family within that block' with no m enumerated, while §7.1 l.340 carries one frozen winner per entry into the freeze (22 entries on T1, 16 on T6), so the hypothesis count is decided after the look; §8 l.388-393 gives each block its own FREEZE file and claim marker with no ordering rule and no requirement that all three FREEZE files and all frozen configurations (winners, seeds, ensemble members, the 0.05 margin) exist before the first look. Precedent: chemtox_unseen_taxa_plan.md §6 enumerates its family and requires Holm across block x reference pairs for any cross-block statement; LEAD_DECISIONS M6 requires 'one claim model per track, chosen by a rule written in the amendment that uses inner-CV or validation data only'.
verdicts.ruling_text: Before the stamp the amendment names one claim model per block chosen on pool validation only and enumerates the Holm family as (claim model + the other candidate entries) x (the (a) and (b) comparator legs) with m fixed in writing; all three blocks' configurations, seeds, ensemble members and comparator choices are frozen and all three FREEZE files issued by the lead before the first look, no refit or re-selection may occur between the looks, and because T1_test and T6b_test share 232 chemicals any statement spanning blocks additionally needs Holm across the block x comparator pairs.

verdicts.evidence: §6 l.308 states 'Every block is better powered than T2's best (0.011)'. The §6 table's own T6b_test primary MDE at rho=0.9 is 0.0197 (verified identical in t1t6_mde.json), i.e. 1.8x worse than 0.011 and essentially T2's middle block (0.019 per M4_architecture_plan.md §7.1 / chemtox_unseen_taxa_plan.md l.280-282, which give T2 0.011 / 0.019 / 0.021). T6b's co-primary is 0.0213 and its no-shared-reference strata 0.0241 / 0.0232 — all worse than T2's best. §12.2 rule 8 itself concedes T6b may be underpowered, so the file contradicts itself in the direction that flatters its weakest block. On the plan-conflict half: M4_architecture_plan.md §7.2 pre-registered that an underpowered T6b 'is reported as a stratum of T6a, never as a separate claim', while §12.2 rule 8 fixes it as a full block with its own look. The two reviewers split on which is stricter; rule 8 is stricter against post-hoc demotion, the plan is stricter against a third claim opportunity.
verdicts.ruling_text: The sentence is corrected to 'T1 and T6a are better powered than T2's best; T6b is not', and T6b keeps its status as a full block with its own look exactly as §12.2 rule 8 fixes it, but it carries no §15.1 label unless its corrected unit-level MDE supports one and it occupies its own named place in the Holm family; a T6b result below its MDE is reported as a measured null for that block and is never re-described after the fact as a stratum of T6a.

verdicts.id: DURATION-FLOOR-AND-BANDS (merges CT-L10, ST-10-T6-BAND-COMPOSITION, ST-13-BAND-EDGES-AND-ZERO-DURATION, C13-DURATION-FLOOR, C15-274X-SCOPE)
verdicts.evidence: All reproduced from the sealed split, counts only. Degenerate durations: duration_h == 0 in 2 T6a_test rows and 1 T6b_test row; 0 < duration_h < 1 h in 337 T6a_test and 84 T6b_test rows; build_t1t6_split.py applies no lower bound (only notna()). Band occupancy under the MDE script's own cut (compute_t1t6_mde.py l.28-30, BAND_EDGES starting at -0.001, pandas default right-closed): T6a_test lt24 4,522 / 96_168 3,893 / 168_720 4,252 / 720_2160 343 / gt2160 49; T6b_test 964 / 608 / 769 / 50 / 19. The bands are right-closed, so the band labelled '< 24' holds rows at exactly 24 h (T1_test 2,459 and train_pool 13,890 are all exactly 24 h) and silently absorbs the zero-duration rows. §3 publishes only '5,486 below 24 h, 9,983 above 96 h' and 'maximum 26,298 h'; §6 powers only 'all' and 'no shared reference', no band. The 274x figure is T6a's alone: T6a duration_max 26,298 h (273.9x), T6b duration_max 8,035.5 h (83.7x), per t1t6_counts.json, yet §3 and §7.1 attribute 274x to 'T6's test blocks'. Haber's rule (C x t constant, §4.3) is undefined at t = 0, so the designated crude-rule floor cannot be evaluated on part of its own block.
verdicts.ruling_text: Before the stamp the amendment states the minimum admissible duration and drops duration_h <= 0 from all blocks with the count recorded (or specifies in closed form how Haber's rule and the composition layer behave as t -> 0), declares the bands as half-open (0,24], (24,96], (96,168], (168,720], (720,2160], (2160,inf), publishes the per-band row counts for T6a and T6b, pre-declares the short (< 24 h) and long (> 96 h) tails as separately reported strata, states the extrapolation reach per block (274x T6a, 84x T6b), and fixes now that no claim rests on a band with fewer than 50 resampling units.

verdicts.evidence: §4.2 R5 (l.164) is 'TRIDENT head-to-head via its released per-SMILES 10x10-CV errors, never by re-running TRIDENT' and concedes 'TRIDENT's training data overlaps our rows'; §5.2 l.228-229 budgets it as 'r5_trident_released_errors 1 (no fit — a read of the released file over the intersecting SMILES)'. §12.1(a) requires a 'paired CI (cluster bootstrap, 2,000 resamples, unit = the block's resampling unit) excluding 0 against the strongest published method on that block'. A per-SMILES error table from the authors' own random 10x10 CV on their own rows yields no per-row prediction on our blocks, so no paired difference is computable, §4.1 input/row parity cannot hold, and §4.2's own rule that 'strongest published' is 'decided by validation on the pool' cannot be applied to an entry that produces no pool predictions. RESEARCH_PLAN §15.1(i) allows a re-run on our split or on the published benchmark split, not a third construction. §4.3 l.187 nevertheless designates TRIDENT 'the strongest published method for this exact task'. Licence is not the obstacle: docs/licenses.md l.47 confirms Zenodo 10260621, CC BY 4.0, cleared 2026-11-10. Kill rule 3 only covers the case where the file lacks usable errors, not the case where the errors are unpairable.
verdicts.ruling_text: Condition (a) is read only against a published comparator actually re-run here at full parity on the block's own rows (mmoe or gpboost_published, whichever leads pool validation, named in writing before the look); the TRIDENT comparison is a descriptive, non-paired, non-parity cross-reference reported with its split mismatch and training overlap stated, it can never satisfy (a) or carry a §15.1 label, and its released per-SMILES errors are restricted to pool chemicals until the FREEZE file exists.

verdicts.evidence: §3 l.128-133 reports shared-reference row shares 74.4% (T1_test), 53.8% (T6a), 30.9% (T6b) — reproduced exactly from t1t6_counts.json (0.7443 / 0.5382 / 0.3087), with no_shared_reference_rows 2,697 / 6,031 / 1,666 and §6 stratum MDEs 0.0167 / 0.0134 / 0.0241. T2's comparable share was 16-29%. §12.1(h) requires only that the reference-clustered co-primary CI exclude 0 and that the no-shared-reference stratum be 'reported'; §12.1(f)'s 'for that block and stratum' is ambiguous about whether the stratum gates. The frozen protocol for the same workstream is stricter: chemtox_unseen_taxa_plan.md §6 condition (f) requires 'the point estimate keeps its sign on the block's parent_novel stratum, on the no shared reference stratum, and under the reference-clustered CI'. So a T1 label could rest almost entirely on rows whose study is already in training.
verdicts.ruling_text: Condition (f) is split: the difference must exceed the corrected primary MDE on the full block AND keep its sign on the no-shared-reference stratum and exceed that stratum's own rho=0.9 MDE; a claim failing the stratum leg is reported as qualified and labelled 'not separable from publication structure', and any label that passes is explicitly scoped as including shared-publication rows.

verdicts.evidence: §12.1(d) l.511 reads '>= 3 seeds, with all_seeds_better reported' — reporting, not holding. RESEARCH_PLAN §15.1(iii) requires 'the gain holds in >= 3 seeds' and §14.4 requires 'seed variance in CIs'. The frozen protocols of the same workstream are explicit: chemtox_unseen_taxa_plan.md §6 'Seeds 0, 1, 2 for every stochastic model; a claim requires the gain in all seeds (§15.1 iii), per block. A model whose seeds disagree is reported as unstable, not as a winner.' Seed ids are unstated in the amendment; §4.1's parity statement (l.147-155) lists rows, features and auxiliary targets but not seeds, although LEAD_DECISIONS required seed parity explicitly for M2; and §14.4's seed variance in CIs is not implemented — how the 3 seeds enter the paired bootstrap is undefined.
verdicts.ruling_text: Condition (d) reads: seeds 0, 1 and 2 for every stochastic entry including comparators and ensemble members, all_seeds_better must be TRUE for any §15.1 label, the reported point estimate is the seed mean, and the paired bootstrap is run per seed with the per-seed CIs reported beside the seed-mean CI.

verdicts.evidence: grep of the whole amendment for 'micro', 'macro', 'primary metric', 'percentile', 'two-sided' and 'sided' returns nothing; RMSE appears only in the selection rule (l.338-342) and the MDE. §12.1(a) specifies 'paired CI (cluster bootstrap, 2,000 resamples, unit = the block's resampling unit)' with no confidence level, no sidedness and no interval method. The frozen T2 protocol fixes all of it (chemtox_unseen_taxa_plan.md §6: 'Primary metric per block: micro-RMSE on its primary (in-domain) endpoint, in log10(mol/L)'; 'percentile intervals'; 'paired bootstrap on identical rows against every comparator, two-sided'; plus a named secondary list). In a confirmatory design that leaves micro/macro weighting, the secondary list, the level, the sidedness and the interval method open after the look.
verdicts.ruling_text: The primary metric is micro-RMSE in log10(mol/L) on the block's rows as in the frozen T2 protocol §6; macro-RMSE by chemical and by species, MAE, R-squared, bias and percent within 1 log unit are reported and never claimed; every CI is a two-sided 95% percentile cluster bootstrap with B = 2,000, paired on identical rows.

verdicts.evidence: The premise holds but one sub-claim is overstated. Confirmed: R5 covers only intersecting SMILES (§5.2 l.228-229); Haber's rule is undefined at t = 0 and T6a/T6b contain 2 and 1 zero-duration rows plus 337 and 84 sub-hour rows; §12.1(g)'s 'beats' is undefined (point difference or CI). Overstated: 'T1_test and T6b_test share 0 chemicals with train_pool, so a carry-forward baseline has no in-pool duration for those chemicals' — the cluster hold-out does make held-out and pool chemicals disjoint on test_cas, but nearest-observed-duration carry-forward is a T6-only baseline (§4.3 l.190-192) and T6a_test chemicals ARE in the pool (1,175 chemicals, retained clusters), so it is well defined on T6a and undefined only on T6b. Nothing in the amendment pre-registers the evaluation row set for any comparator, so the subset each comparison is read on can be chosen after the look.
verdicts.ruling_text: For each comparator the amendment states before the stamp the rows it is evaluated on and the declared fallback for rows it cannot score; the confirmatory comparison is always read on the full block with the unscoreable comparator's rows filled by its declared fallback, any intersection-only comparison is secondary and labelled as such, and condition (g) requires a point difference in the candidate's favour against every parity comparator.

verdicts.evidence: §5.1/§5.2 give T1 both xgboost_emb and rf_emb as searched entries plus trivial_global_mean, trivial_per_species_mean and trivial_per_chemical_mean as fixed. §5.3 gives T6 only xgboost_emb_dur among tuned simple baselines (no rf entry at all), and §5.4's fixed list has trivial_global_mean only — no per-species mean, no per-chemical mean. So condition (b)'s 'strongest simple baseline' on T6 rests on a single tuned tree family, and the trivial-context rung is thinner than on T1. RESEARCH_PLAN §14.3 requires the trivial-context rung in every table and §15.5 item 4 forbids baselines being weakened, removed or under-tuned. §4.2 R4 also names 'rf' as an arm that must receive the embedding, but T6 has no rf arm for that clause to apply to.
verdicts.ruling_text: T6's fixed list gains trivial_per_species_mean, trivial_per_chemical_mean and a per-species x duration-band mean (all free), rf_emb_dur is added either as a searched entry inside the 128 cap or as a fixed entry, and condition (b) on T6 is read against whichever simple baseline leads pool validation, named in writing before the look.

verdicts.evidence: Three confirmatory paths carry an unresolved 'or'. §10.2 l.466-470: 'MolFormer-XL ... is the intended source, with ChemBERTa-2 as the alternative; neither is used until its weight licence is verified', with a Chemeleon fallback and no precedence rule; because §5 counts one configuration budget per entry, a second embedding source would silently double entries 3, 4, 5, 10 and 11 on T1 and the corresponding T6 entries. §4.2 R1 l.160 is 'LightGBM/XGBoost with monotone_constraints' — library unfixed. §12.2 rule 3 l.525-527 says condition (a) falls back to 'the strongest remaining published comparator (mmoe or gpboost_published)' with no rule for choosing between them.
verdicts.ruling_text: Precedence is fixed now — MolFormer-XL if its weight licence clears, else ChemBERTa-2, else the in-tree Chemeleon fallback, one source only, recorded with its licence date before any fit, and trying a second source is a new entry whose 32 (T1) / 16 (T6) configurations count against the declared 544; R1's library is fixed to one of LightGBM or XGBoost in the same addendum; and the kill-rule-3 fallback between mmoe and gpboost_published is resolved by pool validation under §4.2, never by choice after the look.

verdicts.evidence: unseen_taxa.py l.65 ADORE_STRUCTURE_CLASSES = ('organic','organic_multicomponent'); l.109 sets in_adore_domain from chem_structure_class; l.664 inside mde() restricts to dom = block[block['in_adore_domain']]. compute_t1t6_mde.py l.23 sets part['in_adore_domain'] = True for every row, so the restriction is bypassed. Quantified by joining chem_structure_class to the sealed split (metadata, no labels): in-domain share is T1_test 86.68%, T6a_test 58.98%, T6b_test 74.73%, train_pool 77.68% — i.e. 41% of T6a's MDE rows are inorganic or organometallic, outside the basis on which T2's 0.011 / 0.019 / 0.021 were computed. More rows means a smaller MDE, so the §12.1(f) gate is loosened relative to the T2 convention the same paragraph invokes, and §6's direct comparison with T2 is not like-for-like. The module pin is intact (sha cf1493c6... equals chemtox_unseen_taxa_pins.json module_sha256), so this is a caller-side choice, not a pin breach, and the amendment never mentions the flag. Compounding: T2's primary metric was defined on the in-domain endpoint while the amendment defines no metric at all, so the evaluation row set remains open after results.
verdicts.ruling_text: The amendment must disclose that in_adore_domain is forced True so no applicability-domain restriction is applied, state that T2's figures were computed on the organic-only subset and are therefore not directly comparable, report the domain-restricted MDE alongside the unrestricted one, fix now whether the claim is read on all rows or on the in-domain subset, and let the stricter of the two MDEs govern condition (f).

verdicts.evidence: The arithmetic is internally correct within each stated scope and the searched caps are exactly the lead's. Verified by enumeration: §5.1 has 12 searched entries x 32 = 384; §5.2 is 1+1+2+1+1+1+1+1+1+1 = 11 across 10 entries, so 'T1 total 395 across 22 entries' is right; §5.3 has 8 searched entries x 16 = 128; §5.4 is 1+1+2+1+1+1+1+1 = 9 across 8 entries, so 'T6 total 137 across 16 entries' is right; 22+16 = 38; 384+11+128+9+12 = 544. LEAD_DECISIONS M4 update and M4_architecture_plan.md §8.2 both set 'T1 384 searched configurations, T6 128, plus fixed baselines; every configuration counted', so no cap is exceeded. What C9 correctly spots is that 395+137 = 532 while the declared grand total is 544, because the 12 ablation fits are in the grand total and in neither per-track total, and §5.6 wires those same figures into the registry as the drift check. C9's proposed remedy (restate the per-track totals as 401 and 143) is one valid fix; one sentence is enough, so this is not a revision requirement.
verdicts.ruling_text: The 12 ablation fits sit outside the 384 and 128 searched caps as fixed fits of the single selected ted configuration and inside the declared grand total of 544, so the per-track totals of 395 and 137 are search-plus-fixed totals only; the searched caps stay at exactly 384 and 128 with no entry exceeding 32 (T1) or 16 (T6), no family re-screened, a failed fit still consuming its slot, the 12 ablations not growing if the fallback cuts ted to 8 configurations, and the realised count including failures and discarded configurations reconciled against these five figures in the write-up and on every registry row.

verdicts.evidence: M4_architecture_plan.md §8.2 phase P5 sized 22-30 GPU-h (cap 32) for '16 configurations x 3 folds = 48 jobs' and P6 8-12 GPU-h for MMoE. The amendment carries those figures over unchanged (§5.7 l.264-265) while the fit count has roughly quadrupled: ted is 32 configurations x 4 folds on T1 plus 16 x 3 on T6 = 176 fits, and mmoe likewise 176 fits against 8-12 GPU-h (about 4 minutes per fit). rx_chemprop is explicitly a GPU entry (§5.1 row 5) with 32 x 4 = 128 fits on T1 and appears in no budget line at all. §5.7 does carry a pre-declared fallback (ted to 8 configurations if the smoke exceeds 30 min/job, repeated as kill rule 1), which mitigates but does not cover mmoe or rx_chemprop. An unachievable budget is the most likely route to a mid-campaign renegotiation, which §5.6 and kill rule 1 exist to prevent. Disk is not an issue: df shows 179 GB free on /, above the 60 GB floor.
verdicts.ruling_text: Before the stamp §5.7 is replaced by a per-entry fit count and a per-entry GPU-hour ceiling that includes rx_chemprop, with a total ceiling; if the ceiling is reached the pre-declared fallback to 8 configurations per track applies automatically and is recorded, and no budget is renegotiated after any validation number on either track exists.

verdicts.evidence: §8 l.391-393 reserves the three blocks 'from today ... by any workstream' by reference to chemtox_t1t6_split_v1.parquet only, and the amendment's preamble says it edits no other file. grep of docs/plans/sota_campaign.md finds no chemtox entry: its 'Reserved unseen blocks (lead, 2026-11-09)' section lists sonde_newsites and ea_england_allocation, and 'Reserved unseen blocks added 2026-11-10' lists M2 Test-S, M5-F France, M1 StreamPULSE and M7 P2. A project-wide obligation over a shared ECOTOX frame is therefore invisible to every other workstream. Reviewers split on severity (note vs should_fix); the stricter reading applies because the obligation is cross-workstream.
verdicts.ruling_text: At the stamp the lead adds T1_test, T6a_test and T6b_test to sota_campaign.md's 'Reserved unseen blocks added 2026-11-10' section, naming chemtox_t1t6_split_v1.parquet with its sha256 005f7957... and the row counts 10,548 / 13,059 / 2,410, with the standing instruction that no workstream trains or tunes on those result_ids and that any overlap is reported to the lead as counts.

verdicts.evidence: ls -la sentinel/models/chemtox/ shows __init__.py, evaluate.py, features.py and tabpfn_model.py at -r--r--r-- while gpboost_model.py is -rw-rw-r-- (5,392 B, 2026-10-24 22:13). grep -c gpboost on docs/preregistration/bioassess_x_freeze_candidate.json returns 0, and no SHA256SUMS file lists it. So the amendment's §1 l.6-7 ('or by the M5 BioAssess freeze (chemtox/{__init__,evaluate,features,tabpfn_model}.py, gpboost_model.py)') and §11 l.496-498 ('that file is covered by an existing freeze and is not edited') are unsupported for that one file, and the unsupported claim is the stated reason for leaving a known-wrong citation in live code: gpboost_model.py l.11 reads 'Bio-QSARs 2.0: Unlocking a generic modeling approach for species sensitivity predictions' while M4_architecture_plan.md l.202 records the Crossref-verified title 'Bio-QSARs 2.0: Unlocking a new level of predictive power for machine learning-based ecotoxicity predictions by exploiting chemical and biological information'. Other agents are editing this repo now, so nothing protects the file or the correction.
verdicts.ruling_text: The claim that gpboost_model.py is covered by an existing freeze is struck from §1 and §11; either the lead names the freeze and hash list that covers it, or the one-line citation is corrected under the lead's change control and the file is then sealed 0444 with its hash recorded in the rulings file, and the commitment to use the verified L6 title in every write-up stands either way.

verdicts.evidence: §4.2 R4 (l.163) states 'Every comparator gets the concatenated embedding block ... parity requires it for R1-R3, rf, xgboost and the published configurations'. §4.3 (l.172-180) states the ADORE published RF/XGBoost use 'verbatim published configurations' and GPBoost uses 'hyper-parameters verbatim from the authors' released _without_DEB models'. A verbatim published configuration fed an extra concatenated foundation-model embedding is no longer verbatim. The enumerations follow §4.3, not R4: §5.2 lists rf_published_adore 1, xgboost_published_adore 1, gpboost_published 2 with no embedding-fed twin, and §5.4 the same. Since §12.1(g) turns on which comparators 'received the same inputs, auxiliary targets and rows', the unresolved contradiction decides after the fact which arms count as parity-matched. R4's 'rf' clause also has no T6 entry to attach to (see T6-BASELINE-LADDER).
verdicts.ruling_text: §4.3 governs for the published arms: they stay verbatim, without the concatenated embedding, and are reported as published-form comparators only, while R4 parity applies to R1-R3 and to the re-tuned rf/xgboost arms, which are the arms condition (g) is read against; any embedding-fed published twin the lead wants must be enumerated as extra configurations inside the caps before the stamp.

verdicts.evidence: The amendment's position is the governing one, not the outlier. chemtox_unseen_taxa_plan.md §6 states in terms: 'The replicate floor is NOT a difference threshold and is not used as one: it bounds the absolute RMSE any model can attain, so requiring a candidate to beat a published comparator by more than 0.649 log units on insects would have made a claim unreachable for a reason unrelated to evidence (delta review W-D-7, over-correcting W-M4U-2)', and the same section declines to declare a practically-relevant threshold. The amendment §6 l.310-316 says exactly this. The two artefacts the reviewer cites are the inconsistent ones: the T2 plan's §2 table carries a 'Floor for a claim' column of 0.649 / 0.437 / 0.402 that its own §6 text contradicts, and the helper docstring (unseen_taxa.py l.660-661) says 'or below the block's replicate floor, whichever is larger'. So the finding is refuted as stated, but a one-line clarification is still worth recording so the two readings are not cited side by side in the paper.
verdicts.ruling_text: For T1 and T6 the corrected MDE is the only difference gate and the replicate floor is reported solely as absolute-RMSE context, as chemtox_unseen_taxa_plan.md §6 already rules; the T2 table's 'Floor for a claim' column and the unseen_taxa.mde docstring are superseded on this point, and this sentence is quoted in any write-up that compares T1/T6 with T2.

verdicts.evidence: §5.6 l.253-256 justifies counting shared entries twice because 'each track is a separate fit on a different training pool'. There is only one pool: t1t6_counts.json has a single train_pool block of 59,729 rows, and §7.1 defines both T1's 4 cluster-group folds and T6's 3 duration-band folds inside it. The arithmetic (384+11+128+9+12 = 544 across 38 entries) is unaffected; only the stated reason is wrong, and the honest statement is that 512 searched configurations are developed on the same 59,729 rows.
verdicts.ruling_text: The clause is restated as 'both tracks search inside the same 59,729-row pool under different fold structures; shared entries are counted once per track because each track selects its own winner', with the total of 544 unchanged.

verdicts.evidence: Independently re-verified, so the lead need not redo it. File sha256 b9326d49aca711f0ceeec1362c21883030a94f83dd6971a2db15cba1babc9a9e matches and the file is unchanged across this review (565 lines, 42,287 B). All eight §2 hashes reproduce on disk; the cluster CSV and the sealed split are 0444; the sealed split has exactly the five declared columns and 85,746 rows and is genuinely label-free. Every one of the 12 §6 MDE values matches t1t6_mde.json and all 12 record target_blind_identical = True. H4 reproduces exactly (17,418 usable / 672 chemicals / 479 species, 16,590 uncensored, 14,951 wet / 2,467 dry, BCF 14,388 / BCFD 2,467 / BAF 563, sd 1.4079, 588 in the universe / 456 in the pool, bcf1_mean the value column, trim [-2,7] removing 42 rows). H2 = 11,719 reproduces with value+smiles and H3 = 225,081 with value+smiles+uncensored. Licences match docs/licenses.md l.47-48. The T2 class exclusion is a genuine superset of T2's blocks and no frozen artefact is opened by the builder. Caps arithmetic 384+11+128+9+12 = 544 across 38 entries is internally consistent and within the lead's caps.

points.point: The disclosed T6 extrapolation decision: the training pool is in-window only, so T6 selection can extrapolate at most 2x while the test blocks reach 274x; the alternative of putting part of the long tail into the pool was rejected (§3, §7.1).
points.ruling: Uphold the design choice — keeping the long tail out of the pool is correct and conservative — but rule that the disclosure as written is false and must be corrected before the stamp. The amendment must state the duration coverage of every row set separately (primary, auxiliary, pretraining), apply the AUX-LEAK exclusion restricting every T6 auxiliary row to 24 <= duration_h <= 96, state the real maximum labelled duration seen in training, and withdraw the §1 'structurally handicapped comparator' argument unless that restriction is in force. Per-band results for the pre-registered bands are a mandatory deliverable of every T6 look; bands with fewer than 50 resampling units (720-2160 h and > 2160 h on both blocks) are descriptive only; the headline is scoped to the bands in which the sign holds; and no write-up quotes the 274x range without the > 720 h strata beside it and without stating the per-block reach (274x T6a, 84x T6b).
points.reason: The 2x-versus-274x disclosure only protects anything if the training set carries no long-duration information, and it does: 138,341 chronic rows on train_pool chemicals, 84,812 of them outside 24-96 h and 72,900 above 96 h on 973 chemicals, max 26,298 h — identical to T6a's maximum — with 11,773 chronic rows in the same (CAS, species, duration) cell as a T6a_test row. Without the restriction the claim would rest on a shape the model had in fact seen. The long tail that justifies '274x' is only 49 rows in T6a and 19 in T6b, while 4,522 T6a rows are below 24 h and 3,893 sit in 96-168 h, so per-band reporting is what stops a near-boundary win being presented as long-range extrapolation. All three reviewers converged on this; the stricter half of each is taken.

points.point: The 544-configuration total (384 searched T1 + 11 fixed + 128 searched T6 + 9 fixed + 12 ablations, across 38 entries) against the §8.2 caps.
points.ruling: Accept 544 as the declared total and 384 / 128 as the searched caps, with four binding additions: (i) the 12 ablation fits sit outside the searched caps as fixed fits of the single selected ted configuration and may not grow if the pre-declared fallback cuts ted to 8 configurations; (ii) the per-track figures 395 and 137 are search-plus-fixed totals and do not include the ablations, which is why they sum to 532 rather than 544; (iii) a second embedding source, a re-screen of any family, or a screen-then-refit pattern is a new entry whose 32 (T1) / 16 (T6) configurations count against the total; (iv) the realised count including failures, discarded configurations and timed smokes is reconciled against these five figures in the write-up and carried on every registry row. Do not accept any expansion after a validation number exists on either track.
points.reason: The enumerations check out by hand (12 x 32 = 384; 11 fixed across 10 entries; 8 x 16 = 128; 9 fixed across 8 entries; 6 ablations per track; 22 + 16 = 38 entries), the searched counts are exactly the lead's caps in LEAD_DECISIONS and plan §8.2, and comparators receive the same per-entry budget as candidates, which is what parity needs. The consistency reviewer is right that 395 + 137 = 532 against a declared 544 and that §5.6 wires those figures into the registry as the drift check, but this is a presentational gap closable by one sentence, not a cap breach. The open edges the stats reviewer names — the undeclared embedding-source choice and the screen-then-refit pattern the ADORE phase used — are the only routes by which the count could actually grow, so they are closed explicitly.

points.point: T5 (cross-source transfer) blocked on the EnviroTox licence; TRIDENT Zenodo record 10260621 cleared so reference R5 is admissible.
points.ruling: Uphold both. T5 is recorded as blocked, not skipped, and stays listed as blocked in RESULTS.md; no EnviroTox file is retrieved, cached or overlap-audited until written permission from the rights holder is entered in docs/licenses.md, and if permission later arrives T5 is pre-registered as a new amendment before any EnviroTox row is read, so the overlap audit against the spent blocks happens before the data lands. No write-up claims cross-source or curation-pipeline generalisation. R5 is admitted as a licensed data read only and is coupled to the R5-NOT-PAIRABLE ruling: it cannot carry claim condition (a), and its per-SMILES errors are restricted to pool chemicals until the FREEZE file exists.
points.reason: Both licence entries verify exactly against docs/licenses.md l.47-48 (TRIDENT CC BY 4.0, access open, 35.7 MB of a 10 GB cap, weights and source not downloaded; EnviroTox has no terms page, an all-rights-reserved notice and no locatable download). Blocking T5 removes a leakage surface rather than creating one, and recording it as blocked preserves the honest denominator campaign rule 3 requires. The residual risk sits entirely on the R5 side: the admissible file is a label-derived per-chemical error table from a model whose training data overlaps our sealed rows, so admissibility as data is not admissibility as the paired comparator, and reading it over the sealed blocks' chemicals before the look would expose a difficulty ranking of sealed chemistry.

points.point: Lines in the file requesting a ruling, and the status of T6b.
points.ruling: There is no 'ruling requested' line: the only candidate (§10.2 l.465, REACH/ECHA) merely restates a standing lead ruling and needs no action. The lead should therefore not read the file as having flagged its own open questions, and should treat the five blocking findings above as the open points the author did not raise. On T6b: keep it a full block with its own look as §12.2 rule 8 fixes, since that is stricter against post-hoc demotion than plan §7.2's fallback, but tie its §15.1 label to the corrected unit-level MDE rather than to the row-level 0.0197, give it its own named place in the Holm family, and report a sub-MDE result as a measured null for that block.
points.reason: grep of the amendment for 'ruling requested', 'open point' and 'decision requested' returns nothing, and the file presents itself as complete — which is why the omissions matter more than they would in a draft that flagged them: the spent-ADORE subtraction and the auxiliary-row filters are each asserted as handled in prose (l.25-26, l.446-449) while being absent from the builder and from §10.1. On T6b the two reviewer positions conflict (report-as-stratum versus full block); rule 8 is chosen because allowing a block to be demoted after its number is known is the larger forking path, and the third-claim risk it creates is closed instead by putting T6b in the single Holm family and by gating its label on the corrected power.

missed.section: §4.1 parity statement and §7.1 'Ensembles' against the §5.2 / §5.4 enumerations
missed.issue: The amendment twice binds itself to ensembling parity — 'if a candidate is an ensemble, the strongest simple baseline is ensembled the same way with the same member count' — but no matched baseline-ensemble entry is enumerated anywhere in the caps, and §5.6 freezes the five configuration figures on every registry row so they cannot drift. missed.evidence: Amendment l.153-154 and l.347-348 state the parity requirement. §5.2 l.229 enumerates only 'ensemble_mean 1 · ensemble_decorrelated 1', both defined in §7.1 as combinations of the frozen candidate winners; §5.4's T6 fixed list contains no ensemble entry. Precedent: LEAD_DECISIONS_20261110.md M1 section approves 'E2 with the matched baseline-ensemble control E2-B' as a named entry with its own budget.
missed.suggested_ruling: Two further fixed entries, ensemble_mean_baseline and ensemble_decorrelated_baseline, built from the strongest simple baselines with the same member count and the same 0.05 margin rule, are added to §5.2 before the stamp and counted inside the declared total; no §15.1 label is available for an ensemble candidate on any block on which the matched baseline ensemble was not built and reported.

missed.issue: No reproduction-fidelity tolerance is pre-registered for any published comparator, although this workstream's own precedent required one and the project's hard threshold for M4 states one. MMoE in particular is a re-implementation ('re-implemented over our endpoint families as the strongest published multi-endpoint architecture') with no check that it reproduces anything the authors reported, and under the R5 ruling it is the entry most likely to end up carrying condition (a). A weak re-implementation is a weak comparator, and nothing in the file would detect one.
missed.evidence: grep of the amendment for 'reproduc', 'fidelity', 'tolerance' and 'within ±' returns only the §2 builder row, the §3 A.2 remark and the §9 H4 sentence — no comparator tolerance. §4.3 l.184-186 for MMoE; l.172-180 for the ADORE and GPBoost published arms. Contrast RESEARCH_PLAN §15.2 'M4 primary: ... reproduced baseline within ±0.03 of 0.927' and chemtox_test_plan.md §2, which pinned the reproduced published baselines with their CV values. docs/licenses.md and §10.2 confirm TRIDENT's released files are available, so a published reference point for R5 exists but is not used as a fidelity check either.
missed.suggested_ruling: Every published comparator must reproduce a published reference number on a published or CV basis within a tolerance written into the amendment before the stamp (±0.03 log units for the ADORE RF/XGBoost arms, and for mmoe and gpboost_published a stated reference figure and tolerance or an explicit statement that none is available), and a comparator that misses its tolerance is reported as a failed reproduction and cannot carry condition (a) or (b).

missed.issue: The decorrelated ensemble admits any member within 0.05 RMSE of the best single model, which is about five times T1's declared primary MDE of 0.0097 and more than twice T6b's 0.0197. The margin is fixed before the look, so this is a disclosure rather than a forking path.
missed.evidence: Amendment l.344-348 ('within a declared margin of 0.05 RMSE of the best single model, with the member set fixed before the test look') against §6's table (T1_test primary MDE 0.0097, T6a 0.0085, T6b 0.0197, all verified in t1t6_mde.json).
